newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU edges towards farm price agreement.
newsitem.headline: EU edges towards farm price agreement.

text.p: European Union farm ministers on Wednesday broadly supported a compromise 1997/98 (July/June) price package from the Dutch EU Presidency, but various details remained to be settled, EU officials said.
"We should get agreement this afternoon after some minor changes," a Dutch spokesman said.
"The reaction was reasonably positive," a Commission spokesman said during a break in the meeting. EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler made no comment.

But Germany and a number of other countries were against any commitment to future cuts in compensation payments to cereals farmers and wanted to change the wording of the text to say that cuts were "not necessary" instead of "premature."
Fischler, claiming that cereals farmers are over-paid, has proposed a 1.4 billion Ecus cut so as to free funds to help beef producers whose herds have been hit by mad cow disease.
Sweden and Finland were trying to obtain a permanent, instead of one-year, exemption for the minimum size of their barley offered into intervention stores.
Germany, Britain and Spain had problems with Denmark's request to apply environmental conditions to set-aside payments, saying this could push up costs.
Members were still trying to squeeze concessions on cotton (Greece), flax (Belgium), milk (Spain and Italy), beef (France), sheepmeat (Italy), wine (Austria) and animal transport (Britain).
Officials said Spain had the most objections but agreement was still expected on Wednesday afternoon.
Ministers were due to resume discussions at 1030 GMT.
